correctness.rationale: At x=y=0 only the constant axial drift −b remains; the third variational coordinate has zero derivative, and the first two coordinates form the stated 2×2 block. Eliminating v gives u''+(a+c)u'+a(c+z₀−bt)u=0. The exponential gauge and affine rescaling have exactly the stated h,q,τ; the Airy Wronskian gives the nonzero linear functional C_B and its one-dimensional kernel, including when Ai(s(0))=0. The derivative term in v dominates u by ±√(bt/a), and the Airy exponents give the signed rates. Eventual norm monotonicity on the growing branch is justified without differentiating an unspecified error: the exact logarithmic derivative is [a u(v−u)−c v²+(bt−z₀)uv]/(u²+v²), which is asymptotic to √(ab t) by the component slope. On finite intervals the unscaled norm is bounded, and it eventually increases without bound; the first threshold therefore exists for small ε and lies at large time. Put W=√U_L and t=W²+pW+r. In (2/3)√(ab)(t−τ)^{3/2}−ht−L the W² coefficient is √(ab)p−h, and the W coefficient is √(ab)(r−τ+p²/4)−hp. Canceling both gives the stated constants; the remaining O(log W) log-norm error shifts time by O(log W/W), using the derivative asymptotic or evaluating at brackets offset by fixed constants. Liouville's formula uses the trace −a−c along any interval on which the flow is defined.
residual_risks: The initial unit direction is fixed off the decaying line; the expansion is not uniform as it approaches that line. A numerical root at two log levels is not proof of the earliest threshold, and neither the proof nor the numerical checks gives a nonlinear exit law.

value.rationale: The model is established, and the escaping axis offers a concrete contrast with the usual emphasis on bounded dynamics and volume contraction. The result determines the exceptional initial direction and quantifies its opposite generic behavior up to an additive o(1) in the linearized departure time, not just a qualitative instability or a leading Airy exponent. This gives a precise test for derivative-level departure in a natural case where no finite standard exponential rate describes the orbit.
residual_risks: The value is orbitwise and linearized; it does not establish a nonlinear exit law, compact attractor, or statistically typical Lyapunov behavior.
